_note: EASY -- the default, and the direct descendant of AIPlaytest.SCRIPT (PLAN.md 12.2a).
THE OPENING IS THE PROJECT OWNER'S OWN SCRIPT, RULE FOR RULE, in the order they
wrote it: two villagers to berries, one to stone, one to wood, the fifth starts a
house; the two drop-off camps beside the resources they serve; gold, then the age;
two more villagers, a mill and a field; then a house, a tower, a barracks and five
swordsmen. What changed is not the plan but what drives it -- every step used to
carry a TIMEOUT IN TICKS and was abandoned when it expired, which is how p2 gave up
on a barracks 73 wood short and died holding 950 (BUGS.md). A rule has no timeout.
It waits.
EVERY RULE CARRIES A CONDITION THAT GOES FALSE ONCE IT IS SATISFIED. Rules are
re-evaluated every think interval and the first match wins, so a rule that stayed
true would fire again and again -- five houses, five barracks. `fewer_than` counts
FOUNDATIONS and PRODUCTION QUEUES for exactly this reason: 'I have already started
one' has to read as 'I have one', or the AI orders another every half second while
the first is being built.
THE FARM COMES BEFORE THE SECOND WAVE OF VILLAGERS (project owner, 2026-09-11: they
'need to age up and build a mill + field at a higher priority'). Berries hold 80 and
are stripped inside the first minute, so past the opening the ONLY renewable food is
the farm -- and a villager costs 50 food while a swordsman costs 60. Training more
mouths before building the thing that feeds them is how a bot ends a match holding
four figures of wood, gold and stone and two digits of food, which is exactly what
four seeds measured on 2026-09-11. advance_age was already above the train rule for
the same reason (see ai_hard.json); the mill and the field now are too, and there
are two fields rather than one because one does not carry seven villagers.
WHY THE OPENING GATHER RULES ARE CAPPED AT AGE 1. The standing orders (AISystem)
already put every idle villager on the poorest resource, which is a better rule
than any fixed split once the economy is running. These four exist to shape the
FIRST minute -- berries before wood, a stone gatherer before anybody needs stone --
and would otherwise fight the standing orders for the rest of the match.
DIFFICULTY, per AI_Player_difficulty.md: focus on building and defending; attacks
after 5 minutes of game time, then keeps going; ages to 2; one tower.
THE CLOCK WAS HALVED ON 2026-09-11, 6000 ticks to 3000, on the owner's ruling that
'bots are too slow over all'. Ten minutes is a long time to wait to be played with.
ARMY CAPS RISE WITH DIFFICULTY (project owner, 2026-08-27), and every one of them
is bounded by POPULATION rather than by taste. A unit is 1 pop, a town centre
gives 10 and a house 5, so the house count in each file has to carry the army the
same file asks for: Easy's 3 houses is a cap of 25 against 7 villagers and 10
swordsmen. Raise a cap without raising the houses and TrainCommand simply refuses
-- a bot that stops training for no visible reason.
THE 5-MINUTE TRIGGER IS A CLOCK, AND THAT IS NOT THE THING THE OWNER RULED OUT.
A per-step timeout ABANDONS A GOAL because the world was slower than a number
somebody guessed -- that is the defect. A global clock that decides when aggression
unlocks abandons nothing and does not depend on how far the gold is; it is a
handicap, deliberately expressed in time, and it is what makes Easy easy.
BUT IT IS A CONQUEST CLOCK, AND THREE OF THE FOUR GAME TYPES ARE NOT CONQUEST, so
`mode_after_ticks` moves it per game type. Trophy is 0: standing on your own dragon
is defending, this profile's whole stated focus, and waiting five minutes to start
means five minutes of the one unit whose death loses the match standing alone. King
of the Hill is 900 -- a KotH match is won at 9,000 points and a side holding the
hill alone scores 3 a tick, so the FASTEST POSSIBLE MATCH IS 3,000 TICKS and a bot
on the conquest clock arrives after the trophy has been handed out. It stays a
handicap on the two modes that are still conquest.
AND `mode_at_least` IS THE HALF THAT ACTUALLY MAKES THE HILL A CONTEST, added after
the clock alone changed nothing measurable. An easy v easy King of the Hill run put
soldiers on the hill at t5621 -- 9.4 minutes -- with the clock already down at 900:
barracks at t4030, the fifth swordsman at t5540, attack at t5580. It was never the
clock, it was the FIVE SWORDSMEN below. That number is about surviving a fight at
somebody's base; the hill is empty ground that pays by the tick, where a lone scout
out-scores an army still in the barracks and can walk away again. So both modes ask
for {} -- go with whatever you have -- and 'whatever you have' cannot be 'nothing',
because _issue_attack refuses to issue with no military to send.
